subject: Clarify: model-improvement restriction + EU residency evidence for ClearWell pilot
messages:
From: Alyssa Mendez <alyssa@clearwell.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwell.io
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot legal/controls questions — model use + residency

Logan — thanks again for the demo this week. Procurement asked me to get written confirmation on a few items before we can issue a PO for the pilot. Short list below — can you confirm and send any evidence you have? We need this inside two weeks.

1) Can Redwood prevent use of our traffic to improve or train models (no model-improvement for any requests we send)? We need a contractual commitment and an operational proof flow.
2) EU residency: for pilot traffic from our EU users, can you guarantee processing and backups stay in EU-only infrastructure (or provide a clear export path)?
3) Subprocessors: updated inventory and any onshore/offshore distinctions.
4) Prompt/response ownership: we need an explicit clause that the customer retains IP and output rights.

I've attached the procurement questionnaire and our standard DPA redlines for reference (procurement-questionnaire.xlsx). Please loop in legal and privacy as needed — cc'd procurement.

Thanks,
Alyssa Mendez
Head of Integrations — ClearWell Labs
alyssa@clearwell.io
+44 20 7123 4567
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Mendez <alyssa@clearwell.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot legal/controls questions — model use + residency

Alyssa — great to hear. Short answers up front, then attachments and next steps.

TL;DR: We offer an account-level "Model Improvement Restriction (MIR)" setting that, when enabled, marks traffic as excluded from model-improvement pipelines and from telemetry buckets used for product model training. We can support EU-only processing for pilot traffic and provide a subprocessor inventory + SOC2 report. Attached: redwood-dpa-draft-v2.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-202704.csv, SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2026.pdf.

Details / proposed operational evidence:
- No-learning (MIR) scope: when that option is enabled for your account, all API events and conversational artifacts are flagged as "no-learn". These records are excluded from any training or fine-tuning queues and from analytics pipelines used for model improvement.
- Evidence we can provide: audit log snippet showing MIR flag on requests, export of the filtered request set, and a signed attestation from our privacy team.
- Residency: we can pin your account to EU-only serving nodes and storage (Azure/GCP regions in EU). For extra assurance we offer:
  * EU-only serving + backups retained in EU
  * On-demand SFTP export to an EU-hosted endpoint you provide (for escrow/export requirements)
  * Customer-managed KMS (bring your own key) for encryption-at-rest where required
- Prompt/response ownership: Redwood's standard proposal is that customers retain IP and output rights for prompts and generated responses; Redwood retains operational telemetry rights necessary to run the service (health, fraud prevention) but will not assert derivative ownership when MIR is enabled.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Legal/Privacy to review and propose a short DPA amendment I can send to you (I attached a draft).
2) If procurement needs a DocuSign packet, we can generate a DocuSign link for signature once the redlines are agreed.
3) Rishi — can you add the audit log snippet + attestation we can share? Kimberly — any contract language we should pre-populate?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call if that helps accelerate.

— Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Mendez <alyssa@clearwell.io>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot legal/controls questions — model use + residency

Alyssa / Logan — looping in a brief proposed clause we can add to the DPA to address ClearWell's asks. This is a short-form suggestion to reduce back-and-forth:

"Model Improvement Restriction. Vendor agrees that, upon Customer's written instruction and account configuration enabling the Model Improvement Restriction (MIR), Vendor will not use Customer Data (including prompts, responses, or derived artifacts) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Vendor's machine learning models. Vendor will segregate MIR-marked data and exclude such data from model-training pipelines, analytics used to produce novel model parameters, and third-party training transfers. Vendor may retain minimal operational telemetry necessary for security and billing, provided such telemetry does not contain Customer content in a form that would permit training.

Evidence and Residency. Upon request, Vendor will provide: (a) a signed attestation confirming MIR is enabled for Customer's account; (b) an extract of audit logs demonstrating the MIR flag assignment for a representative window; and (c) documentation of geographic routing and storage locations for Customer Data. For EU-only residency, Vendor will document the cloud regions in which processing and backups occur and offer on-demand export of Customer Data to an EU endpoint provided by Customer."

A couple of open items for legal ops: retention window for audit exports (suggest 90 days by default; can extend for a fee), and whether on-shore-only subprocessors are required or if contractual controls suffice. Rishi — can you confirm the mechanics of the audit export and the attestation text?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Alyssa Mendez <alyssa@clearwell.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwell.io, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot legal/controls questions — model use + residency

Thanks Logan / Kimberly — that language looks good as a starting point. Procurement is comfortable with the MIR approach and the attestation items. A couple of final asks before we route for signature:

- Can you confirm the retention window for the audit extract (we need 90 days minimum; please confirm you can produce a CSV extract covering that period).
- For EU residency please provide the exact cloud region names (e.g., GCP - europe-west1) in the attestation so our security team can verify.
- Please include the SOC2 Type 2 report and the subprocessor CSV in the DocuSign packet.

If you can send a DocuSign link with the draft DPA + SOC2 + subprocessor inventory by Monday EOD our procurement lead can sign and issue the PO next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — cc'ing procurement for tracking.

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Mendez — Head of Integrations, ClearWell Labs
procurement@clearwell.io
